title: How to automate your sales pipeline with AI
description: Learn how to automate your sales pipeline with AI across prospecting, research, meetings, outreach, CRM updates, and pipeline reviews.
introduction: To automate your sales pipeline with AI, you need more than a tool that writes emails or scores leads. Sales work rarely lives in one place: the account is in the CRM, the relationship is in email and meetings, the useful signal is on LinkedIn or a company website, and the next action is often still in someone’s head.

Strawberry is a browser with built-in AI agents. It gives you a familiar workspace where an agent can learn from your tabs, work across your apps, draw on meetings and files, research the public web, and remember useful context over time. Strawberry calls the agent working alongside you your companion.

That is different from both a chatbot that stops at an answer and a sales tool that automates one narrow slice of the job. Strawberry can connect the work across prospecting, account research, meetings, outreach, follow-up, CRM updates, and pipeline decisions. The context can carry from one step into the next instead of disappearing between tools.

Some of the most ambitious teams are already using Strawberry to automate time-consuming sales work and take on workflows that would previously have been too manual to attempt. You do not need to build that whole system on day one. This guide will show you what is possible, help you find a useful place to begin, and explain how a first win can grow into a much more powerful way to run sales.

sections.title: Where to start with AI sales automation
paragraphs: Strawberry can help across the whole sales journey, but the best first task depends on what is happening now. You might find promising new customers, research an account and find a way in, get ready for tomorrow’s meeting, or send personalized outreach that sounds like you. If you already have something else in mind, start there.

Not sure which would be most useful? Ask Strawberry to recommend a first win from your open tabs, connected apps, and the context it already has. If there is not much to work from yet, it can suggest a useful app to connect—such as your email, calendar, or CRM—and explain what that would unlock. You do not need to connect everything or complete a setup project before doing useful work.

The focused Strawberry skills linked throughout this guide give your agent useful starting points for each job. They are not rigid sales methodologies: your companion can adapt them to the result you need and the way your team already works.

skills.context: Use this guide to choose the most useful Sales workflow from the work already in front of you.

sections.title: Work with Strawberry in small loops
paragraphs: You do not need a perfect prompt. Give Strawberry a real goal, let it take a first pass, and respond as you would to a capable teammate: say what works, what feels off, and what you want to try next. For bigger or more subjective work, begin with a small result—one account brief, a handful of prospects, or a few outreach messages—then build from there.

Your feedback becomes useful context. Over time, your companion can get to know your qualification bar, preferred sources, writing style, level of detail, CRM fields, and the way you like to review work. Once the two of you have shaped a repeatable approach, save what works as a skill so the next run starts further ahead.

sections.title: Find the right customers and reach out like yourself
paragraphs: When the market, segment, territory, or account universe is still unclear, map the landscape first. A market map can define the relevant universe, expose whitespace and concentration, compare regions or verticals, and show where prospecting should focus without pretending the result is already a qualified lead list.

When you need new pipeline, Strawberry can work from a description of the customer, an ICP document, or examples of accounts you already win. It can search sources such as LinkedIn and company websites, explain why each prospect fits, and bring the result back to a sheet, CRM, dashboard, or chat.

Valuable sales signals often live outside standard databases. Strawberry can investigate niche directories, public websites, and older databases to uncover relevant evidence, while keeping the source behind each finding.

Try a small, varied set first and give your agent feedback before going wider. If you already have the companies, enrich the list instead. When you are ready, it can prepare and send personalized outreach in your voice, starting with representative messages and adding a sequence when follow-ups would help.

skills.context: Define the target market, account universe, whitespace, concentration, and where prospecting should focus.
Calibrate a small sample, then build a sourced and qualified customer list.
Add verified contacts and agreed qualification fields to an existing list.
Send personalized outreach in the user's voice, starting with representative messages and adding a sequence when useful.

sections.title: Research accounts and prepare for real conversations
paragraphs: A powerful first loop is research, preparation, conversation, and follow-through. Tell Strawberry which account or conversation matters. It can pull together the account record, recent thread, attendees, company pages, relevant LinkedIn context, prior notes, and fresh signals, then turn them into a concise brief with sources and useful questions.

A typical AI research flow searches the public web and summarizes the pages it can retrieve. Because Strawberry is an agentic browser, it can investigate more like you would: open the real source, follow links, search within sites, move across tabs, and keep digging when the first answer is incomplete. It can also work with relevant pages and apps you already use instead of relying only on whatever you paste into a chat.

skills.context: Research an account, contact, relationship, and credible way into the conversation.
Turn current calendar, relationship, account, and web context into a concise meeting brief.

sections.title: Carry the context from the meeting into follow-up
paragraphs: The same context that helps before a meeting becomes even more useful afterwards. Strawberry can transcribe the conversation without adding a meeting bot. Once the transcript or notes are ready, your companion can prepare a sales debrief, follow-up, next actions, and suggested CRM updates—all grounded in what was actually said.

If the next step needs more than an email, your companion can also turn the account and meeting context into a customer-facing one-pager, deck, tailored page, or interactive asset built around the next decision.

You stay in control of what happens next. Reviewing a recap does not mean sending the email, sharing an asset, or changing the CRM. Once you approve the work, Strawberry can finish the follow-through without another round of copying.

skills.context: Capture the conversation without a meeting bot and turn it into a reliable record.
Turn the conversation into a sales debrief, grounded follow-up, CRM changes, and next actions.
Turn the approved account and meeting context into a customer-facing asset for the next decision.
Review and apply approved CRM changes with the source and target record visible.

sections.title: Turn your pipeline into the next best move
paragraphs: Connect the CRM your team already uses and Strawberry can work with the records there instead of relying on an export or another round of copy-paste. It can combine deal stages with recent meetings, email activity, commitments, missing information, and fresh account signals.

That turns a pipeline review into more than a CRM summary. Strawberry can spot stalled deals, neglected follow-ups, and the actions most likely to move something forward, then propose updates for you to review. It can also assess whether volume, quality, stage balance, concentration, timing, momentum, and loss risk plausibly support your stated goal without imposing a generic coverage ratio.

When coverage is weak, the review recommends the next separate workflow: map the market if the segment or account universe is unclear, or find more qualified customers if the target is already understood. A review-only request does not launch broad research automatically.
Start with a review you can talk through together. Once the team trusts the signals and recommendations, your companion can prepare it regularly as a Routine.

skills.context: Review pipeline health and turn it into a small, evidence-backed next-action plan.
Clarify the market, segment, territory, or account universe when coverage problems begin upstream.
Build more qualified pipeline after the target market is sufficiently understood.

sections.title: Turn what works into a team advantage
paragraphs: A shared Sales companion can get to know the whole team: the customers you care about, the way you qualify accounts, the tone you use, the meetings you have had, and the skills that make the work run smoothly.

When someone improves a useful skill, teammates can benefit without rebuilding it from scratch. The companion becomes a living home for the team’s sales context and ways of working—something people can actually use, enjoy, and improve together, not another playbook sitting unread.

skills.context: Bring a useful individual workflow into the shared Sales companion so teammates can use and improve it together.

sections.title: Grow one useful win into a sales operating system
paragraphs: Getting started is not a one-time checklist. After a useful account brief, connect preparation to follow-up. After a helpful pipeline review, improve how the CRM stays current. After a strong prospect sample, save what your companion learned about a good fit. Each useful loop can make the next one better.

As the pieces begin to work, connect them. A trusted workflow can become a skill, a shared team capability, or a Routine that runs at the right moment. The goal is not automation for its own sake. It is a sales operating system that gives the team more time, carries context forward, expands what the team can take on, and still leaves people in control.
If you are new to Strawberry, open the Getting Started with Sales skill and choose one useful piece of work. You can begin with the context already in front of you and build from there.
